To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effect of the first meal after a 12-h overnight fast on glycemia in people with type 2 diabetes is dependent on the carbohydrate content and composition.

a low-carbohydrate, high-protein diet is effective in reducing weight, improving glycemic control and reducing the need for diabetes medications in people with type-2 diabetes, with a greater effect than the low-fat diet.

the effect of the first meal after the overnight fast on the subsequent glycemic response was significantly influenced by the carbohydrate content of the meal and that a carbohydrate restriction in the initial meal after the overnight fasting was associated with a significant improvement in the postprandial glucose response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel carbohydrate-based materials for the delivery of biologically active compounds.
the effect of a low-carbohydrate diet on blood sugar and insulin levels.
the effects of a carbohydrate restricted diet on glycemic control, body composition, cardiovascular disease risk factors, and quality of life in people with type two diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence supports the use of a carbohydrate-restricted diet in the management of obesity.
a low-carbohydrate diet, as a first line of therapy in the treatment of patients with diabetes, should be considered as a viable alternative to a high carbohydrate diet.
the consumption of carbohydrates is a necessary part of a healthy and balanced diet.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ketogenic diet is safe and may be beneficial for the treatment of refractory epilepsy.
carbohydrate restriction, in the context of a balanced diet, is a viable option for improving glycemic control.
the effect of carbohydrate restriction on glucose control in people with T2DM depends on the amount of carbohydrate in the meal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a diet with a high proportion of carbohydrates is not the best diet for the prevention and management of type 2 diabetes.
a low-carbohydrate, high-fat diet is not a good choice for people with diabetes.
a high-carbohydrate, high-fiber diet may be the best option for people with type 1 diabetes who are looking to lose weight.
